newsitem.title: UK: Airtours says holiday demand, bookings rise.
newsitem.headline: Airtours says holiday demand, bookings rise.

text.p: British-based holiday operator Airtours Plc said on Thursday that an encouraging trading performance in the year to date supported its expectation of further improvement in 1996/97 after it posted increased profits from all markets in 1995/96

In a statement delivered at its annual meeting, the group said its British unit Airtours Holidays had posted winter bookings 10 percent ahead of last year, and its summer bookings had continued to run "significantly ahead of last year".
The group said its British travel agency chain Going Places had increased its share of the market in both the winter and summer seasons after an expansion of its retail network.

Meanwhile in the Scandinavian market, where the group owns companies including the major Spies brand, winter 1996 bookings have been running 80 percent ahead of last year, or 32 percent excluding Spies, with initial summer bookings also ahead.

"Airtours in is good condition and our principal markets are showing signs of improvement in demand which has resulted in improved load factors in all of our businesses," chairman and chief executive David Crossland said.
He added due diligence was underway for the planned purchase by Airtours and its industry partner Carnival Corp of Italy's Costa Crociere SpA, the largest cruise operator in the Mediterranean.
By 1212 GMT the company's shares were up four pence at 850-1/2, off an earlier high of 860 pence, in a broadly strong London stock market.
